Find discordant barcodes

Source: R/quality_control.R
find_discordant_barcodes.Rd

Finds the barcodes whose log2 fold change is far from that of the other barcodes of the same gene. Discordant barcodes may have off-target effects or a poor knockdown, and can drive a gene to be (or not to be) a hit.

Usage

find_discordant_barcodes(table_treate_vs_control, threshold = 3)

Arguments

table_treate_vs_control

A table with one row for each barcode and at least the columns Barcode, Gene and Log2FC, as returned by compute_metrics or compute_barcode_statistics.

threshold

The number of MADs from the gene median beyond which a barcode is discordant (default 3).

Value

A tibble with the discordant barcodes and the columns Barcode, Gene, Log2FC, GeneLog2FC (median of the gene) and Deviation (distance from the gene median in MADs), ordered by the absolute deviation.

Details

For each gene it computes the median and the median absolute deviation (MAD) of the log2 fold changes of its barcodes; a barcode is discordant when its distance from the median is larger than threshold MADs. When the MAD of a gene is 0, every barcode that differs from the median is discordant, with an infinite deviation.

Use it to inspect the hits, not to filter the barcodes before finding them. The discordant barcodes are found with the same fold changes that the tests use, so removing them is circular: it makes the genes look more consistent than they are and the p-values too small. In shRNA screens it also removes the hairpins that work, when most of the hairpins of an essential gene do not. In the K562 screen (k562_count_table) removing them before find_gene_zscore_hit found fewer essential genes and more non-essential ones. To exclude bad barcodes, use information that does not come from the comparison, for example barcodes that are discordant in several independent screens with the same library.

See also

compute_metrics, filter_by_variance, plot_barcode_trend

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
table <- compute_metrics(object,
    control = "Time3", treatment = "TRT",
    day = "Time3"
)
find_discordant_barcodes(table)
